classification.difficultyReason: Requires interchanging variables, rearranging a linear rule and plotting the function and inverse consistently as reflections in y=x. The sequence is directly modelled; repeated parts and fractional coefficients add no new conceptual demand.

content.prompt: Find the inverse function $g(x)$ of each function $f(x)$. Sketch the graph of each function and its inverse function on the one set of axes and also sketch the line $y=x$.

answer.short:
$g(x)=x-5$.

The two parallel lines are reflections in $y=x$.
answer.worked:
Interchange $x$ and $y$, then make $y$ the subject.

$\begin{aligned}x&=y+5\\y&=x-5\\g(x)&=x-5\end{aligned}$

Sketch $y=x+5$ through $(-5,0)$ and $(0,5)$, and $y=x-5$ through $(5,0)$ and $(0,-5)$. Include $y=x$; the function and inverse are reflections in this line.

spec.description: Three straight lines on common axes, with the function and inverse identified and their intercepts marked.

answer.short:
$g(x)=\dfrac{x+2}{3}$.

Reflect the graph of $f$ in $y=x$ to obtain the graph of $g$.
answer.worked:
Interchange $x$ and $y$.

$\begin{aligned}x&=3y-2\\3y&=x+2\\y&=\frac{x+2}{3}\\g(x)&=\frac{x+2}{3}\end{aligned}$

Sketch $y=3x-2$ through $(0,-2)$ and $(\frac23,0)$, and $y=\frac{x+2}{3}$ through $(-2,0)$ and $(0,\frac23)$. Include $y=x$. The graphs of $f$ and $g$ are reflections in this line.

spec.description: Function, inverse and dashed reflection line on common axes; four intercepts marked.

answer.short:
$g(x)=\dfrac{x-2}{3}$.

Reflect the graph of $f$ in $y=x$ to obtain the graph of $g$.
answer.worked:
Interchange $x$ and $y$.

$\begin{aligned}x&=3y+2\\3y&=x-2\\y&=\frac{x-2}{3}\\g(x)&=\frac{x-2}{3}\end{aligned}$

Sketch $y=3x+2$ through $(-\frac23,0)$ and $(0,2)$, and $y=\frac{x-2}{3}$ through $(2,0)$ and $(0,-\frac23)$. Include $y=x$. The graphs of $f$ and $g$ are reflections in this line.

spec.description: Function, inverse and dashed reflection line on common axes; four intercepts marked.

answer.short:
$g(x)=\dfrac{4-x}{3}$.

Reflect the graph of $f$ in $y=x$ to obtain the graph of $g$.
answer.worked:
Interchange $x$ and $y$.

$\begin{aligned}x&=4-3y\\3y&=4-x\\y&=\frac{4-x}{3}\\g(x)&=\frac{4-x}{3}\end{aligned}$

Sketch $y=4-3x$ through $(0,4)$ and $(\frac43,0)$, and $y=\frac{4-x}{3}$ through $(0,\frac43)$ and $(4,0)$. Include $y=x$. Both graphs meet the reflection line at $(1,1)$.

spec.description: Two decreasing lines reflected in a dashed y=x, with four intercepts marked.

answer.short:
$g(x)=6-2x$.

Reflect the graph of $f$ in $y=x$ to obtain the graph of $g$.
answer.worked:
Interchange $x$ and $y$.

$\begin{aligned}x&=3-\frac12y\\\frac12y&=3-x\\y&=6-2x\\g(x)&=6-2x\end{aligned}$

Sketch $y=3-\frac12x$ through $(0,3)$ and $(6,0)$, and $y=6-2x$ through $(0,6)$ and $(3,0)$. Include $y=x$. Both graphs meet the reflection line at $(2,2)$.

spec.description: Two decreasing lines reflected in a dashed y=x, with intercepts 3 and 6 on both axes.
